title: Kubernetes in a microVM
summary: The vendor’s own guide to two ways of combining Kubernetes with microVMs: a containerd shim and `RuntimeClass` that start each pod as its own VM (marked experimental, with its known blockers listed), or a whole k3s cluster, through k3d, inside one VM. Useful for the concrete details, such as per-pod overhead, the `/dev/kmsg` device the kubelet needs and why Docker’s storage must sit on ext4, but written to sell smolvm.
